leftEvidence.title: David calls it an everlasting covenant

points.label: Covenant setting
points.left: The Davidic promise is explicitly named as an everlasting covenant from David’s later vantage point.
points.right: The chapter does not use the noun covenant, but later Scripture explicitly remembers this promise as covenant with David.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: David · house · Everlasting covenant · ordered · secure · Later Davidic reflection · Promised order · lived complexity
points.right: David · offspring · House · throne · Kingdom · sonship · enduring throne · David builds? → God will build David a house

payload.posture: David’s last words name an everlasting covenant in relation to the earlier house, offspring, and throne promise.
payload.tension: The two sources materially share covenant language or memory, while their parties, setting, action, or literary purpose remain distinct.
payload.title: David calls it everlasting / the house promise is spoken
